Looping in from infra/serving. Quick notes after an initial look at the traces Alex attached: 
- The 5xx is a 502 returned by the model routing proxy (nginx layer) with "upstream prematurely closed connection" patterns in the attached logs. That usually points to the model worker process crashing or hitting a hard memory limit during processing of the batched request.
- 12 x ~700-token items in a single request can blow past memory thresholds for some model variants, especially when reranker does cross-attention between items (worst-case O(n^2) memory).

Immediate mitigations we can try for Finlytics: 
1) Create a per-account routing policy that shards large batches into smaller sub-requests (we can do transparently at the gateway).
2) Increase worker memory limits on a staging pool and run the payload to see whether it's transient.
3) Add a 45sRead/Write timeout bump for this route while we test.

Dev will attach a short SDK snippet that shows an alternative: chunk the batch into groups of 4 and perform parallel calls. Alex - if you can confirm "parallel batching" is acceptable, we'll prepare that as a recommended change.

I'll prepare a staging route and run the example payload against it. Sharing any further logs here.

- Dev

Alex - we reproduced the failure on staging with your payload (thanks for the minimal example). Repro notes: 
- Model variant: mini-rerank-v2 (the variant Finlytics is routed to)
- Single POST with 12 items: worker OOM and process restart observed at ~28s after request start.
- With batch size 4 (3 subcalls) the request succeeded; total elapsed ~= 12s.

I'll attach the SDK snippet (sdk_snippet.txt) that Marissa mentioned in the thread - shows how to chunk and parallelize with the JS SDK and keep the same semantics. We recommend: 
- Chunk size: 4 items per call
- Client parallelism: up to 3 concurrent subrequests
- Server routing: temporarily bump route timeout to 60s while you transition

Alex, if you want, we can enable a per-account transparent sharding policy (server-side) so you don't have to change client code. That will be a short-lived config while you roll out optimized batching. Which do you prefer?

Thanks,
Ethan Park
